answer.diagnosis: A small 3x3 patch near the top-left corner (image rows 1-3, cols 1-3) carries very large first-layer weights (about ±60 to 99) in 17 hidden units. That is far stronger than these units' other off-blob weights. Units 1, 7, 11, 12, 14, 16 and 19 weight the patch strongly positive. Units 3, 5, 8, 10, 17, 20, 23, 25, 30 and 31 weight it strongly negative, even though their weights over the rest of the background are positive. Nothing about blob size is located in that corner, so the units are detecting a corner marker that must have been correlated with the label during training. The genuine size features are separate: centre-surround and ring patterns around the middle of the image (positive discs in units 1, 7, 11, 12, 14, 16 and 19; negative centre with positive surround in units 3, 5, 8, 17, 20, 23, 25 and 31). The fix is to zero the corner-patch weights in every unit, which leaves the size-detecting weights intact.
